content: If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from moisture and light. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Liquid forms of this medication should not be frozen. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Before taking dimenhydrinate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to diphenhydramine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause drowsiness or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Liquid products or chewable tablets may contain sugar and/or aspartame. Exercise caution if you have diabetes, phenylketonuria (PKU), or any other condition requiring you to limit or avoid these substances in your diet. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug. Older adults may also be more susceptible to side effects such as drowsiness, confusion, constipation, or difficulty urinating. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels on all your medications (e.g., allergy or cough-and-cold products) as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., allergy skin tests), potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Symptoms of overdose may include severe drowsiness, seizures, or widened pupils.
